item.description:

It is becoming a tradition for us to host Beginning of Summer & End of Summer Full Day Sunday Pickin’ Parties. We have a full day of live music fun for Sunday September 20th.
2-5PM-Suns of Stars

From live music to art shows, “One World Brewing” is born from the magic that happens when the whole becomes greater than the sum of its parts. item.title: Clouds Of Delusion | Fridays In The RAD Music Series — Fri Sep 18, 6:00 PM — Records in the RAD/The Wedge
item.description:
We have as amazing show lined up for this Friday evening featuring Clouds of Delusion. Show starts at 6pm. Great music, delicious food and cold beverages. Free of everyone and everyone welcome! Clouds of Delusion is an Asheville based Grateful Dead tribute band consisting of high level jazz trained musicians. They are heavily inspired by the music of the Grateful Dead and enjoy showing their love for the music by playing it with their own flare and high energy jams. Records in the RAD in the River Arts District is a thoughtfully curated record store with an eclectic selection of vinyl, both new and used. In addition to records, we also have a music inspired art gallery, which features artwork from Brian, Dylan and Susan Haynes. recordsintherad.com At Wedge Brewing, we got our start in the River Arts District, and therefore hold art and community very close to us. We create beer for the creatives and give them a place to commune. wedgebrewing.com
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Craggy! — Mon Sep 21, 8:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group We'll start at Graybeard Overlook (BRP) and hike on the MST past the Douglas Falls trail, then beyond the Visitor Center, then take the side trail to the Craggy Gardens overlook, and then have our break at the gazebo, which is our turn around. About 7 miles out and back on the MST. Craggy trails: rocky with uneven terrain. Pace approximately 2 mph, at times slower.
Not a dog friendly hike.
**Optional car pool:** Meet at Folk Art Center, **lower parking level** at **8:00**. Trailhead at 8:30.

item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group This route includes the Kenilworth neighborhood and the historically diverse South Asheville neighborhood. We will stop at a historic church and cemetery, as well as Kenilworth Park and Chiles House. We will go up Reservoir Rd to take in the view and get a workout.
**Rating: Moderate+** **Distance:** 5 miles **Elevation:** 670 feet **Surface:** Road **Type:** Butterfly Loop **Pace:** 3 mph on the flats, slower up Reservoir Rd **Gear:** In winter, please bring a headlamp or flashlight. water, snack, poles for the climb **Features:** Neighborhood charm Kenilworth, a little history, and views from the top. Not likely to see bears - but we did see one near this route earlier in the spring. **Dogs:** On leash. **Cautions:** Maintain normal traffic awareness. **Route:** [Kenilworth to Reservoir Rd ](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/map/kenilworth-to-reservoir-road-overlook-d9e74f4?p=-1&sh=ifwm3x).

AVL Writers This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.
For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.
Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.
If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.
If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).
Source: AVL Writers

item.description:
Introduction to Permaculture Design with Jennifer Verprauskus Friday, October 9 | 10 am – 1pm BREG – Core Register Here!
Permaculture is a design approach that works with nature rather than against it, creating landscapes that are productive, resilient, and regenerative. In this introductory workshop, participants will learn the foundational ethics and principles of permaculture and discover how thoughtful design can reduce maintenance, conserve resources, improve biodiversity, and create beautiful, functional outdoor spaces. Through discussion, examples, and hands-on exercises, attendees will explore how to observe natural patterns, understand site conditions, and apply simple design strategies to gardens, homesteads, and residential landscapes. Whether you are a homeowner, gardener, designer, or simply curious about sustainable living, this class provides practical tools for creating landscapes that thrive over time. item.description:
Fall Ecology Walk with Dan Lazar Friday, October 9 | 1:30 – 3pm BRN – Core | BREG – Core Register Here!
Participants will walk through the garden and then head into the Arboretum Forest on easily accessible trails. Along the way we’ll take in autumn wildflowers and the changing hues on autumn’s rich palette of colors apparent on the diverse species of our native trees. We’ll learn how each autumn in Southern Appalachia is different, due in part to this biological diversity and changing climate conditions over the course of the year. This program takes place in the classroom and outdoors. Please come prepared to walk on gentle, yet uneven terrain, and dress appropriately for the weather. Dan Lazar served for many years as the director of education at the Western North Carolina Nature Center, followed by several years as executive director of the Colburn Earth Science Museum.
